result.title: Reading Between the Chapters: A Graph-Free RAG Rebuilt With AI and Human Feedback
result.summary: Many questions about a book can only be answered by connecting passages chapters apart, such as a cough heard three times across a horse's life. We introduce CrossChapterQA, 1,853 such questions over 14 public-domain books. Each question lists the two to six chapters it needs (spanning half the book at the median) and the relation linking them, cites evidence from each, and has two independent reference answers graded blind. We use it to build LadderRAG, which indexes a book as passages, summaries and book-level cards for about $0.41 and answers a question for under a cent. Its first version failed mostly at retrieval. We redesigned it four times, steered by an LLM judge's verdicts and our analyses of failed answers: a design-level counterpart of RLAIF and RLHF in which feedback changes the architecture, not model weights. We also report the two redesigns that made answers worse. On the 191 questions its first version got wrong, the final version retrieves over twice as many required chapters on held-out books (recall 0.36 to 0.79), and ten annotators rate its answers 6.5/10 on average (764 ratings).

AI.brief_summary: 提出 CrossChapterQA：14 本公版书上的 1,853 个需跨 2–6 章（中位跨半本书）的关系型问答，标注所需章节、连接关系与证据；并据此构建 LadderRAG（passage、摘要、书籍卡片三级索引），依 LLM judge 判定与错答分析四次重构架构，也报告两次使效果变差的设计。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「所需章节＋关系」的链式证据标注与必需证据召回率（0.36→0.79）评估方式，可能为 LVR 的多步视觉证据筛选与证据覆盖度量提供可核查的借鉴线索；但属纯文本检索工作，与推理期 latent 状态生成无直接关系。
